newsitem.title: USA: Waigel - Germany wants strong, not stronger dollar.
newsitem.headline: Waigel - Germany wants strong, not stronger dollar.

text.p: German policy makers were united in their view of not wanting a much stronger dollar, German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday.
"We want a strong dollar but not a stronger dollar," Waigel said when asked about the dollar's current level.

On Sunday, Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer also said that the U.S. is interested in a strong but not stronger dollar. Waigel said that the G7 nations had sent a signal to the markets with their communique at the weekend meeting.
"And now we have to wait and see," Waigel said referring to the market's reaction to that statement.
At 1511 EDT/1911 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.7234/38 marks, down from its opening level of 1.7320/30 marks and its 55-month peak of 1.7389 reached in Tokyo trade on Monday.
